title: Normalization commutes with the further purely inseparable extension
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field] and let $C$ be an integral finite-type $k$-scheme [def-pc-integral-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-pc-scheme]. Let $k_1/k$ and $k_2/k_1$ be finite purely inseparable extensions [def-pc-field-extension, def-weil-pbc-finite-purely-inseparable-extension]. For $i=1,2$ put $C_{k_i}=C\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k}\operatorname{Spec}k_i$ [def-pc-fibre-product]; its reduction $(C_{k_i})_{\mathrm{red}}$ [def-weil-pbc-scheme-reduction] is an integral scheme, and let $\nu_i:N_i\to(C_{k_i})_{\mathrm{red}}$ be its normalization [def-sc-normalization], viewed over $C_{k_i}$. Assume that $N_1$ is geometrically normal over $k_1$: for every field extension $L/k_1$, every local ring of $N_1\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k_1}\operatorname{Spec}L$ is an integrally closed domain [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]. Then there is a unique isomorphism $N_2\cong N_1\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k_1}\operatorname{Spec}k_2$ [def-pc-base-change] of schemes over $C_{k_2}$, where the right side maps to $C_{k_1}\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k_1}\operatorname{Spec}k_2=C_{k_2}$ by $\nu_1\times\mathrm{id}$; and $N_2$ is geometrically normal over $k_2$ in the same sense. Under this identification, for every closed subscheme $D_1\subseteq N_1$ [def-weil-closed-immersion], the reduced inverse image [def-weil-pbc-scheme-reduction] of $D_1$ in $N_2$ is $(D_1\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k_1}\operatorname{Spec}k_2)_{\mathrm{red}}$ [def-pc-fibre-product]; in particular, if $D_1$ is finite over $k_1$ [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], this reduced inverse image is finite over $k_2$.

source.place: Tags 0C3N (varieties-lemma-normalization-and-change-of-fields: canonical comparison, isomorphism for separable and universal homeomorphism in general), 038M (varieties-definition-geometrically-normal) and 038O (varieties-lemma-geometrically-normal); the geometric-normality hypothesis on N_1 makes N_1 x k_2 normal, integral and finite birational over (C_{k_2})_red, which upgrades the comparison of 0C3N to an isomorphism for the purely inseparable extension k_2/k_1.

proof.text: Write $X_i=(C_{k_i})_{\mathrm{red}}$. By [lem-pc-homeo-pure-insep], $C_{k_i}$ has the irreducible nonempty space of $C$; reduction makes $X_i$ integral. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-algebraic-normalization-field-change] to the reduced finite-type $k_i$-scheme $X_i$: its componentwise normalization is finite and surjective and is an isomorphism over the dense open normal locus of $X_i$. As $X_i$ is integral, it has one irreducible component, $X_i$ itself, so this componentwise normalization is the given $N_i$; hence $\nu_i$ is finite surjective and $\nu_i^{-1}(U)\to U$ is an isomorphism for every open $U$ of that normal locus. Each $N_i$ is integral, since on an affine chart its integral-closure ring is a subring of $k(X_i)$ [def-sc-normalization]; its local rings are normal domains by [lem-sbc-integral-closure-finite-normal-product].

proof.text: Take a dense normal open $U_1\subseteq X_1$ from step 1. Apply [lem-trf-reduced-inseparable-finite-model] with $W=C_{k_1}$, $X=X_1$, $N=N_1$, $K=k_2$: geometric normality supplies normal local domains on $Y=N_1\times_{k_1}k_2$. It gives a finite surjection $p:Y\to X_2$ with $Y$ integral normal and a dense open $U_2\subseteq X_2$ such that $p^{-1}U_2\cong U_2$.

source.place: Tags 0BXR (normalization), 0C3N (field change), 038M and 038O (geometric normality); finite model and fibre-product assembly

proof.text: The open $U_2$ is normal because it is isomorphic to an open of $Y$, so [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-algebraic-normalization-field-change] gives $\nu_2^{-1}U_2\cong U_2$. Both inverse images are nonempty opens in integral schemes, hence dense. The schemes $X_2,N_2,Y$ are finite type over $k_2$ (the latter two are finite over $X_2$), hence locally Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]. Apply [lem-trf-normal-dense-open-finite-target-extension] to these inverse images over $X_2$ in both directions. The resulting maps extend the inverse isomorphisms over $U_2$; their composites are identities by its uniqueness assertion. This gives $N_2\cong Y$. Any other isomorphism over $C_{k_2}$ is over $X_2$, since the reduction immersion is a monomorphism, and has the same restriction over $U_2$; the same uniqueness assertion makes it equal. For every $L/k_2$, $N_2\times_{k_2}L\cong N_1\times_{k_1}L$ has normal local domains by the hypothesis, proving geometric normality.

proof.text: Under this isomorphism, the inverse image of $D_1$ is $D_1\times_{N_1}Y=D_1\times_{k_1}k_2$ by the fibre-product definition [def-pc-base-change]; taking its reduction gives the required reduced inverse image [def-weil-pbc-scheme-reduction]. If $D_1$ is finite over $k_1$, its base change is finite over $k_2$ by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-morphism-permanence](a). Its affine ring $R$ is a finite $k_2$-module, so the nilradical quotient $R/\sqrt{0}$ is again finite [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism].
